subject: Re: Request: backoff window exception for reserved GPUs
messages:
From: Elena Paredes <eparedes@stargate.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Request: backoff window exception for reserved GPUs
Attachments: request_logs_20261120.csv

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the help earlier this week. We're ramping traffic for our new Summarize+ feature which launches the week of Nov 30 and expected burst patterns are sharper than our normal distribution — multiple concurrent short bursts (5–30s) with only 15–45s idle between batches. Those short idle periods are causing the Reserved GPU backoff policy to move many of our streams into queueing and then into fallback models which spikes tail latency to ~2.5–3x.

This is specifically affecting the reserved pool you provisioned for us (pool-stg-5). Because these are user-facing completion requests, the latency spikes are materially impacting conversion during the pilot. We need an exception for the backoff window behavior for this pool for the next 8 weeks: reduce the backoff grace window from 120s to 10s and allow a temporary soft-priority lane for sustained short bursts.

I attached a CSV with sample request timestamps and p95 latency slices. Can you confirm if this is something Redwood can support without a full re-architecture? If not, what mitigations (short-term) do you recommend?

Elena
Elena Paredes
Head of Infrastructure, Stargate AI
eparedes@stargate.ai

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Elena Paredes <eparedes@stargate.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: backoff window exception for reserved GPUs

Elena — thanks for the detail and for the CSV, that helped. We're seeing the pattern in monitoring too and agree the current backoff window is the primary trigger.

Quick answers:
- Short-term: we can implement a targeted policy change for pool-stg-5 to shorten the backoff/grace window and add a transient priority lane for 4–8 weeks. It will be applied as a policy flag (no infra code change).
- Risks: this reduces the automatic smoothing that protects headroom across tenants; we want to scope to your pool and put explicit headroom limits to avoid noisy-neighbor impact.
- Operational asks: we will need a 24/7 contact for the launch window, and we'll require a signed one-off SLA amendment that caps our liability and defines crediting for missed throughput during the carveout.

I'll pull Lauren in — she'll own the formal proposal and the SLA appendix. Can we do a 30m call Monday to align on exact window, expected qps profile, and contact rotations?

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Dylan — Monday works. Couple more details so you can scope:
- Typical user-facing burst is ~18–26 concurrent requests for 8–22s, then ~30s idle. Peak sustained for ~3–4 hours during promo windows.
- QPS per instance jumps from 1.2 -> 7.8 during bursts.
- We can provide a short-lived extra 2 GPUs if needed but prefer policy change first.

Contact for on-call is myself (mobile: +1 415-555-0128) and our SRE lead (ops@stargate.ai).

Elena

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elena Paredes <eparedes@stargate.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: backoff window exception for reserved GPUs
Attachments: proposed_sla_appendix_v3.pdf

Hi Elena — following our call this morning, attaching a proposed short-term amendment (proposed_sla_appendix_v3.pdf) that reflects the operational compromise we discussed. Summary: 

- Scope: pool-stg-5 only; effective immediately upon signature for 8 weeks (extendable by mutual agreement).
- Behavior change: backoff/grace window reduced from 120s -> 10s for in-flight state transitions; a transient "burst-priority" lane will accept up to 25 concurrent streams with bounded CPU/GPU headroom set at +15% of current reservation.
- Guarantees: we will maintain p99 latency <= 2.0x baseline for the burst-priority lane; if we miss the p99 target in >2 independent 1-hour windows, customer is eligible for a pro-rated usage credit (formula in appendix).
- Safety controls: automatic rollback trigger at sustained CPU/GPU utilization > 90% for 3 consecutive minutes; both sides must acknowledge before we re-enable.

Jonas and I scoped the operational runbook and the rollback thresholds. If you accept, legal will prepare a one-page side letter and finance will add the minimal surcharge for the risk window.

If you'd like to iterate on the credit formula, we can do that in parallel; pushing for sign-off this week to get configuration in place before the Nov 30 traffic spike.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Success (Enterprise), Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

We also want the kickoff runbook call on Monday 29 Nov at 09:30 PST to validate alerting and rollback playbook. Confirmed on-call contacts: eparedes@stargate.ai and ops@stargate.ai.

Elena
